audience: High-school seniors; first-principles teaching, with concrete prerequisite capabilities and taught bridges.
prerequisites: Signed arithmetic, fractions, ratios, powers, linear equations, and coordinate graphs
learning_outcomes: Identify state variables, terms, coefficients, and domains
Evaluate a short synthetic path action with units
Distinguish a local coordinate change from a global loop condition
Compute a composite phase while retaining every factor
Use a finite product analogy before the source construction
Check a specified sector without assuming all sectors were checked
Classify every input as a locked root, theorem, constitutive rule, domain condition, or state coordinate
requested_deliverables: capstone.md with full answers and rubric
assumptions: A topical short course, not a semester per topic. Pacing is 55-minute core lessons plus capstone periods; split dense lessons if actual learner load requires it.
No prior calculus, abstract algebra, university linear algebra, or quantum mechanics unless explicitly taught earlier.
Required core assessments must be solvable with taught finite examples. Clearly label deeper recognition-only extensions.
Markdown is the delivery format; no PDF or Word generation is required.

source_routing.guidance: Retrieve exact topic sources and source-local pointers; use the provided archival files read-only and verify their hashes. Do not rely only on titles or summaries. For experimental topics search the testbench topic and local relevant domain skills.

evidence_rules: Preserve empirical observations, derived implications, inferred structure, mechanisms, reference theory, and unresolved questions as distinct layers.
Read-only sources: no source-data copies, database exports, reindexing, or large arrays. Persist only authored course artifacts, compact provenance, audits, and small clearly synthetic examples.
Cell3 uses ICRS columns [a b c], an intentional negative determinant, and half-open cells [-1/2,1/2)^3. Use x-O_K in affine reciprocal identities.
Use the mature locked geometry and exact source provenance. Historical and corrected numerical branches remain separately labeled; do not silently mix their constants.
Use M_cell=B^T B and R_cell=M_cell^-1; distinguish G_phase, G_eff, reciprocal bases, distance Q, Q_g, and Q_nu.
Gauge-carrier tuples use color-first C_3 direct-sum W_2. A weak-first view needs an explicit permutation.
Do not merge detector parity, A1 carry parity, projective signs, chirality, family labels, primitive lifts, or distinct dyadic and ternary recursions.
Declare nearest-integer half-ties and the corresponding residual interval consistently; the half-open cell ownership rule is a separate operation.
The detail-product identity needs explicit hypotheses on E beyond Q=I-E; retain the product of finite differences.
M19 contains mixed extension branches and is not a premise of M20 core closure. Reconstruct prerequisites from module requires, with the documented audit corrections.

Preserve mature-source claims and accepted integration dispositions separately. In the integration only compiler M03, M07, M08 have direct authority; these compiler labels are not automatically the mathematical-backbone module labels. Preserve the admitted global-form family Z1,Z2,Z3,Z6 and source-local uniqueness claims with explicit contracts.
Treat matching dimensions or graph labels as neither an intertwiner nor a proof. A missing proof body remains a source-reported status with a retrieval gap.

Physical CMB velocity is distinct from phase-transformed vectors; the testbench admitted speed is 369812.50200040644 m/s. The Galactic Center is a visual gauge; do not invent Solar or Galactic short-window dynamics.
A photon-equivalent model energy is not measured transferred energy, and phase is not force. Preserve signed events and the three independent plane-cost levels in the fourteen-row 2026-08-26 bundle.
Cell3 and galaxy-derived cells have separately typed units, metrics, handedness, scales, and normals. Recurrence is an explanatory target, not permission to merge definitions.
Every residual remains a primary coordinate. Transformations are reversible or accompanied by all removed components and reconstruction rules; no outlier deletion or significance-based erasure.
Use tf_gpu_env through C:/ProgramData/anaconda3/Scripts/conda.exe run -n tf_gpu_env python. No package changes without approval.

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define an action specification by its variables, ordered times, terms, coefficient units, domain, boundaries and evaluation rule. Read all four source integrand terms but use a separately declared finite scalar analogue for arithmetic.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Toyq dimensionless, dt=1 TU, k=2 AU*TU, vpot=2 AU/TU. DefineS=sum_j dt[k/2*((q_j+1-q_j)/dt)^2-vpot/2*q_j²], with fixed endpoints and ordered samples. Each term hasaction unitsAU.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For path(1,2,2), list3 state values,2 time intervals, coefficientsk, vpot and declared left-endpoint potential rule. Changingvpot changes the model; changingdt requires recomputing velocity and weights.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: SourceM15 mu, M, kappa, epsilon, U, C, s, boundaries andtime normalization require typed definitions. The toy is not an invented replay of an unavailable full source action packet.

course_map.assessment_target: Compute a composite phase while retaining every factor

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Declare a finite scalar phase analogy after choosing a common trivialization. Retain six independently typed factors UV, light, reg, heavy, cap, induced before taking their product; teach complex multiplication without droppingunit factors.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Ordered factors(i, i,-1,-i, i,1) multiply1. Deleting heavy(-i) yieldsi, so the factor is necessary even though the complete product closes.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Factors(-1, i, i,1,-i, i) multiply1. Deleting cap(-i) yieldsi. Retain the heavy unit1 and every phase label; a unit factor still carries provenance.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A product1 in one synthetic sector does not establish source closure for every admitted sector or give a global determinant-line trivialization.

course_map.worked_example_capability: Use a finite product analogy before the source construction
course_map.assessment_target: Use a finite product analogy before the source construction

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach a one-dimensional complex line with a chosen basis, then tensor six lines and distinguish a section from its scalar coefficient. A trivialization tau:Ltotal->C is extra structure. Use finite basis changes to show why scalar products require this declaration.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Withtau(eUV tensor...tensor einduced)=1, the worked six coefficients give value1. RebaseeUV prime=i eUV:its coefficienti becomes1, total coefficient becomes-i, whiletau(new tensor basis)=i; the physical scalarvalue remains1.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: In the practicepacket rebaseecap prime=-ecap. Itscoefficient-i becomes+i, total coefficient becomes-1, whiletau(new tensor basis)=-1; the final scalar remains1. Preserve the basis change andtau, not just a product of revised coefficients.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Do not replace the source tensor product by six bare scalars until the trivialization is stated. One finite basis example is not a proof that a global trivialization exists.

course_map.worked_example_capability: Check a specified sector without assuming all sectors were checked
course_map.assessment_target: Check a specified sector without assuming all sectors were checked

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach rational arithmetic for source topology under explicit integers A3, A2, C: n3=A3+C/3, n2=A2+C/4, n1=C/72. The dual contract requiresd3, d2 integers andd3/3+d2/4+d1/72 integer. Add an admitted-sector list and test closure only there.

worked_example.task_and_answer: d=(1,0,48),(0,1,54),(1,1,30) each givefractional combination1;(1,1,-42) gives0. ForA3=1, A2=0, C=3, n=(2,3/4,1/24); pairing withd=(1,1,30) is4.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: ForA3=0, A2=1, C=4, n=(4/3,2,1/18); pairing withd=(0,1,54) is5. d=(1,1,0) gives7/12 andfails thedualcontract. If a supplied admitted list has sectorsa, b andphase products1,-1, retain both and report closure fails on b.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Arithmetic membership in this lattice is not independent proof of physical admissibility. Testing only a cannot establish every admitted sector; missing factors or sector definitions are marked unavailable, not filled byassumption.
